subject: Having some difficulty fitting multiple Gaussian Processes in one go

messages.author: f15962d5dfbc3d93
messages.subject: Having some difficulty fitting multiple Gaussian Processes in one go
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm fairly new to Nimble and Bayesian stats in general, and have been picking up a project where someone left off. In particular, I have been trying to do Gaussian Process Regression on a hierarchical model someone has already coded. It makes three outcome predictions for many individuals over time. I have, however, had two issues, both related to the fact that I am fitting multiple GPs rather than just one:
  • The model takes way longer to run than it should because I couldn't figure out how to index the line defining K properly. This means that I have had to program it to calculate covariances with all data points, rather than just those from the same individuals. I believe that this has been significantly slowing down calculation when I try running it with and without this line. I have tried to fix this using techniques such as switching what I am looping over ( for (i in (1:N_data)[n_reshape==n]){... ) but this causes errors such as "Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val): 2 nodes produced errors; first error: Could not evaluate loop syntax: is indexing information provided via 'constants'?", and I had one about dynamical looping but I forgot what generated that.
  • The 'bigger' problem is that I have been unable to get the final likelihood line to work, with the following error: "Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val): 2 nodes produced errors; first error: Error, hit end". I think that this may be due to the indexing of the individual n and outcome, leading to a matrix of dimension 1x1xMxM, rather than MxM (where M is the number of data points that individual has) as desired. However there doesn't seem to be a way to flatten things in Nimble that I can find at the moment, so I don't really know how to deal with this.
The relevant GP part of the model is as follows:

#Gaussian Process
  for (output in 1:N_cols){
      for (n in 1:N_patients){
        gp_rho[n,output] ~ dnorm(0,5)
        gp_alpha[n,output] ~ dnorm(0,5)
        gp_sigma[n,output] ~ dexp(1)
        for (i in (1:N_data)[n_reshape==n]){
          for (j in (1:N_data)[n_reshape==n]){
              K[n,output,i,j] <- (gp_alpha[n,output]^2) *exp(-((t_reshape[i]-t_reshape[j])^2)/(gp_rho[n,output]^2))
          }
        }
        L[n,output,1:N_data,1:N_data] <- K[n,output,1:N_data,1:N_data] + (gp_sigma[n,output]^2) * identityMatrix(N_data)
      }
    }
 

   
  #observations:
  for (data in 1:N_data) {
    y_state[data] <- #code that generates the predictions which is secret but definitely works don't worry about this

  }
  for (n in 1:N_patients){
    for (output in 1:N_col){
      y[n_reshape==n & out_reshape == output] ~ dmnorm( y_state[n_reshape==n & out_reshape == output], L[n, output, t_reshape[n_reshape==n & out_reshape == output], t_reshape[n_reshape==n & out_reshape == output]])
    }
  }

For clarity: N_data is the number of data points, N_patients are the number of individuals, N_col is basically just three (number of outcomes), t_reshape is the time input for data, out_reshape indexes outcomes (1,2, or 3) for each point, n_reshape indexes individuals for each point.

I would really appreciate any help, advice or general tips on solving these issues (or pointing out anything else that might be wrong/inefficient in my code).
Thanks.

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Having some difficulty fitting multiple Gaussian Processes in one go
parts:
Hi Victor,

Thanks for posting the question. I think there are some basics of what is allowed in nimble model code that will help get you started on the right foot. If you haven't already spent time with our User Manual and r-nimble.org, that might also be helpful. 

Code like "for (i in (1:N_data)[n_reshape==n])" won't work.  Model code declares hierarchical model (aka graphical model) relationships among nodes and does not support all of R syntax for doing so. A common way to pick out subsets would be to use nested indexing like this: (I am dropping the output and j indices in order to simplify the example)

for(n in 1:N_patients) {
  for(i_ind in 1:N_data[n]) {
    K[n, i[n, i_ind] ] <- some_function(...)
   }
}
To make this work, you need to set up N_data as a vector of the known number of data (i.e. sum(n_reshape==n)) and provide N_data in the constants lists to nimbleModel.  Also you need to create the indexing matrix i such that for patient n, the elements i[n, i_ind] for i_ind = 1 ... N_data[n] give the indices you want to make the model declaration for. I am not sure I have this arranged as you need because I am not completely sure of the intention of your code, but I'm hoping this idiom will give you something to work with. An indexing vector or matrix should be provided to nimbleModel in the constants list (not the data list) if it is known in advance.

Also it will not work to do something like
y[n_reshape==n & out_reshape == output] ~ dmnorm(...)
Use of the logical indexing won't work and also elements that compose a vector following a dmnorm (or any non-scalar distribution) must be contiguous. A nested indexing idiom would be something like

y[n, 1:N_col[n] ] ~ dmnorm(...)

or possibly

y[ N_start[n] : N_end[n] ] ~ dmnorm ## to make one long vector of all the y pieces

and you'll have to also make some kind of nested indexing arrangement for the arguments to dmnorm.  (Again N_col and/or N_start and N_end would need to be set up in R and provided in the constants list).

I hope that helps.  If you try building up from these ideas and get very stuck again, please go ahead and post another question.

Perry

Hi Perry,

Thanks very much for the fast assistance with this. I have been staring at this for most of today, and seem to have managed to calculate K using this method, but am struggling a little bit more with getting L and y to work.
The current code I am working with is:
  for (n in 1:N_pat_with_points){

L[i_n[n], output, 1:i_j[n,output], 1:i_j[i_n[n],output]] <- K[i_n[n], output, t_reshape[j[i_n[n],output,1:i_j[i_n[n],output]]], t_reshape[j[i_n[n],output,1:i_j[i_n[n],output]]]]+ gp_sigma[i_n[n],output]^2 * identityMatrix(i_j[i_n[n],output])
      y[j[n,output,1:i_j[n,output]]] ~ dmnorm( y_state[j[n,output,1:i_j[n,output]]], L[n, output, t_reshape[j[n,output,1:i_j[n,output]]], t_reshape[j[n,output,1:i_j[n,output]]]])
    }
  }
Newly introduced variables include N_pat_with_points, which is a bit like N_patients was before, but removes patients which didn't have any points associated with them (this was causing some issues), and i_n indexes these. So a for loop n in 1:N_patients before is basically the same as n in 1: N_pat_with_points using i_n[n] but skipping these. Similarly j[n, output,i_ind] indexes the position of the  i_ind'th point for the nth individual's output'th output. I also use i_j[n,output] to indicate how many of these points there are.

I am getting the following error: "Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val): 2 nodes produced errors; first error: getSymbolicParentNodesRecurse: dynamic indexing of constants is not allowed in t_reshape[j[n, output, 1:i_j[n, output]]]. Try adding the dynamically-indexed constant as data instead (using the data argument of nimbleModel)". So it seems as though, roughly in line with the issues I had before, the problem is with the use of 1:i_j[n,output]? If this is the case then I'm not really sure how to deal with this - as at some point I have to consider the points as a group (rather than go through them as a for loop) in order to add the diagonal gp_sigma and take the dnorm. Indexing in this way seems to sometimes work and sometimes not work and I don't really understand when this is. Maybe this isn't the issue and I am just lost?

I would greatly appreciate any further help here,

Thanks,
Victor

Hi Victor,

Yes, `mean` has to be a vector (1-d array) and `cov` has to be a matrix of dimension at least 2x2. Is it possible that for some value of `n` that `i_j[i_n[n],output]` is not 2 or more?

-chris
